title: The court sits
caption: Fifteen chairs, five Justices. The Supreme Court never hears an appeal as a whole court: the Constitution says it is properly made up when at least five of its Justices sit, and the rest of the bench stands empty.

check.question: This appeal turns on what a section of the Constitution means. How many Justices must hear it?
check.explain: Five is the minimum for the court to be properly constituted. Where an appeal is about the interpretation of the Constitution or a breach of fundamental rights, or the court is using its original jurisdiction, the panel is seven.

title: In public
caption: The galleries round three sides of the room are there to be sat in. The Constitution requires the proceedings of a court, and the announcement of its decision, to be held in public — justice is meant to be watched being done.

title: The appeal is called
caption: The court's officers, at the desk below the bench, call the case. It has already been through at least one court before this one: an appeal reaches the Supreme Court from the Court of Appeal, and from nowhere else.

check.question: Which court do appeals to the Supreme Court come from?
check.explain: The Supreme Court alone hears appeals from the Court of Appeal. A case that starts in a High Court has to go through the Court of Appeal first.

title: Counsel are heard
caption: A lawyer for each side addresses the bench in turn. Look for a witness box and there is none: this is an appeal, so the argument is over what the law means and whether the court below applied it properly, not over what happened.

title: The court rises
caption: The Justices leave to decide. That part happens out of this room and out of sight, but not without a limit: every court must deliver its decision in writing within ninety days of the final addresses.

title: Judgment
caption: The court returns. Each Justice gives an opinion in writing, or says in writing that they adopt the opinion of another who has — so a Justice who disagrees can say so, and say why.

check.question: The five Justices split three to two. Whose view is the court's decision?
options: Neither — the appeal is heard again
check.explain: The decision of a court of more than one judge is the opinion of the majority of its members. The two in the minority still give their opinions; they simply do not carry the day.

title: The last word
caption: There is nowhere to take the case from here. No appeal lies from a decision of the Supreme Court to any other body or person, which is what makes this the room where an argument about the law in Nigeria finally ends.

check.question: Who can hear an appeal against a decision of the Supreme Court?
check.explain: No appeal lies to any other body or person. The section leaves one thing untouched — the President's and a Governor's power to grant mercy to a convicted person — but that is a pardon, not an appeal.
